title: Dry Riser
activity: Dry riser pipework, valves and test
status: Draft spot check from ITPs – for agreement

questions.q: Pipe galvanised, with a bracket within 1 m of each mechanical joint?
Is each landing valve ≥750 mm above FFL, labelled "DRY RISER OUTLET" and the pipe bonded?
Is the air release valve above the highest landing valve and isolation valves padlocked open?
Ask the fitter: What did it test to and for how long? Could they answer?
questions.source: SuperPrime site practice – a fitter who can't answer is a red flag

questions.q: Air test 0.5 bar for 15 min, then water test 12 bar for 10 min, witnessed by MPX?
Is the outlet cabinet complete, glass intact and surround made good?
Inlet box at ground level accessible, labelled "DRY RISER INLET" and the door/glass intact?
questions.source: Argus dry riser ITP AFP-00002 – installation

questions.q: Permit to fill issued before the water test?
questions.source: Argus dry riser ITP AFP-00002 – MPX permit to fill

questions.q: Pipe brackets tight, pipe plumb, fire stopping complete where it passes through floors?
questions.source: Argus dry riser ITP AFP-00002 – installation

notOk.t: Pipe support more than 400 mm from the penetration
Outlet not rotated to final position / too low for the core opening
Cabinet glass broken or wrong door wording
Making good around the outlet poor

ask.q: What test have you done on this riser?
ask.a: Air 0.5 bar for 15 min, then water 12 bar for 10 min, witnessed by MPX.

ask.q: What height are the landing valves?
ask.a: At least 750 mm above FFL, labelled 'DRY RISER OUTLET'.

ask.q: How far are the brackets from the joints?
ask.a: Within 1 m of each mechanical joint.
